text.p: Ralcorp Holdings Inc said Thursday its private-label cereal operations, which had been under pressure from price cuts by branded products, have returned to profitability.

"Today's earnings highlight a return to profitability of our Ralston Foods cereal operation," Joe Micheletto, Ralcorp chief executive officer, said in a statement. "Since the sale of our branded cereal business to General Mills (Inc ) on January 31, 1997, the company has been restructuring its remaining cereal operation to reflect what is now a singular focus on private label."
Ralcorp said its cereal volume grew by two percent for the third quarter ended June 30, marking the first volume improvement in its private label cereal business in over a year.

"We also believe that the recent stabilization in our private label cereal volume and additional planned cost cutting initiatives should provide opportunities for further operating profit growth in cereal," Micheletto said.

Earlier, Ralcorp reported earnings for the third quarter ended June 30 of $0.09 a share, up from a year-ago loss of $0.11 before a charge. Third quarter results surpassed the First Call consensus of a loss of $0.04 a share.
Ralcorp said its consumer foods operating profit increased in the third quarter on overall improvements at Bremner crackers and cookies and Beech-Nut baby food.

Beech-Nut baby food posted strong volume and operating profit in the third quarter, aided by grocery trade purchases in advance of Beech-Nut's price increase in July 1. This was partially offset by increases in advertising and promotion spending.
Bremner crackers and cookies improved sales and profit in the quarter on stronger volume and an improved product mix.
